title: Air Fryer French Fries
description: Crisp golden air fryer French fries with fluffy centers, light seasoning, and far less oil than deep-fried potatoes.
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, about 1 1/2 lb total
1/2 tsp fine sea salt, plus more to finish
instructions: Scrub or peel the potatoes, square off rounded sides if desired, and cut them into evenly sized sticks about one-quarter inch thick.
Rinse the cut potatoes under cold water, then soak them in a large bowl of cold water for at least 20 minutes to remove surface starch.
Drain the potatoes thoroughly and dry every surface with clean towels; lingering water creates steam and prevents a crisp exterior.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F, then toss the dry potato sticks with oil, salt, garlic powder, and smoked paprika until lightly coated.
Arrange the potatoes in a loose layer in the basket, cooking in two batches when necessary so hot air can circulate around every fry.
Air-fry for 10 minutes, pull out the basket, and shake vigorously to turn and separate fries that have begun sticking together.
Continue cooking for 8 to 12 minutes, shaking every 4 minutes, until the fries are deeply golden with crisp edges and tender centers.
Transfer immediately to a wide bowl, season while hot, add parsley if desired, and serve at once with ketchup before the crust softens.
tips: Russet potatoes produce the fluffiest centers.
Dry the soaked potatoes extremely well.
Cook in batches instead of crowding the basket.
commonMistakes: Uneven cuts brown at different rates.
Wet potatoes steam instead of crisping.
Leaving fries unshaken causes pale contact spots.
substitutions: Use avocado or canola oil.
Replace paprika with black pepper.
Use sweet potatoes and begin checking earlier.
storage: Refrigerate cooled fries for up to 3 days.
Reheat at 375°F in the air fryer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Do not microwave if crisp texture matters.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Air Fryer Chicken Breast
description: Juicy air fryer chicken breasts with a savory paprika-herb crust and a dependable quick-cooking method.
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 6 to 8 oz each
Lemon wedges and chopped parsley, for serving
instructions: Pat the chicken completely dry, then gently pound the thick ends so every breast has a mostly even thickness and cooks at the same rate.
Mix salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, and black pepper in a small bowl until the seasoning is evenly distributed.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F while rubbing the chicken with olive oil and coating all sides evenly with the prepared seasoning blend.
Place the breasts in the basket smooth-side down with space between them, working in batches rather than overlapping or crowding pieces.
Cook for 7 minutes, turn each breast with clean tongs, and continue cooking for another 5 to 9 minutes depending on thickness.
Check the thickest section with an instant-read thermometer and remove each piece as soon as it reaches a safe internal temperature of 165°F.
Rest the chicken on a clean plate for 5 minutes without cutting, allowing carryover heat and redistributed juices to keep the meat moist.
Slice across the grain, spoon any resting juices over the meat, and serve with lemon and parsley while the seasoned crust is still warm.
tips: Even thickness is more important than identical weight.
Use a thermometer instead of guessing doneness.
Rest before slicing to retain juices.
commonMistakes: Cooking straight from frozen gives uneven results.
Crowding blocks air circulation.
Continuing far past 165°F dries the meat.
substitutions: Use avocado oil instead of olive oil.
Replace oregano with Italian seasoning.
Use chicken tenderloins and shorten cooking time.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days.
Freeze cooked chicken for up to 3 months.
Reheat gently until the center reaches 165°F.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Air Fryer Salmon
description: Tender, flaky air fryer salmon with lemon, garlic, paprika, and crisp seasoned edges in under twenty minutes.
ingredients: 4 center-cut salmon fillets, 5 to 6 oz each
1 lemon, half sliced and half cut into wedges
instructions: Check the salmon carefully for pin bones, remove any with clean tweezers, and pat the top and skin completely dry with paper towels.
Combine salt, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and black pepper, then brush the flesh lightly with olive oil and season it evenly.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F and lightly oil the basket only if its manufacturer recommends doing so for delicate fish.
Place the fillets skin-side down in a single layer with space between them, then lay a thin lemon slice over each seasoned portion.
Cook without turning for 7 minutes, then begin checking because thin tail pieces can finish several minutes before thick center cuts.
Measure the thickest point and remove salmon at 145°F for fully cooked fish, when the flesh flakes readily but remains moist inside.
Move each fillet carefully with a wide spatula and rest for 2 minutes, leaving any skin stuck to the basket behind if preferred.
Finish with chopped parsley and fresh lemon juice, then serve immediately while the edges are lightly crisp and the center stays tender.
tips: Choose fillets of similar thickness.
Dry fish browns better than damp fish.
Begin checking before the suggested maximum time.
commonMistakes: Overcrowding creates uneven airflow.
Turning fragile salmon can break it.
Overcooking squeezes moisture from the fish.
substitutions: Use melted butter instead of olive oil.
Replace parsley with dill.
Use trout fillets and monitor early.
storage: Refrigerate cooked salmon for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently at 325°F until hot.
Freeze tightly wrapped portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Air Fryer Steak
description: Air fryer ribeye steaks with a browned peppery crust, juicy center, and melting garlic-herb butter.
ingredients: 2 boneless ribeye steaks, about 1 inch thick
instructions: Remove the steaks from refrigeration for 20 minutes, pat them very dry, and trim only unusually thick exterior pieces of hard fat.
Stir softened butter with grated garlic, parsley, and thyme, then chill the mixture briefly while preparing and cooking the steaks.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, rub both sides of each steak with avocado oil, and season evenly with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Set the steaks in the hot basket with clear space between them, making sure no edge folds upward against the side of the basket.
Cook for 5 minutes, turn with tongs, and continue for 4 to 7 minutes while checking the center with an instant-read thermometer.
Remove at about 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140–145°F for medium, recognizing that temperature rises slightly during resting.
Place a spoonful of garlic-herb butter on each steak, loosely tent, and rest for 5 minutes so the juices redistribute before cutting.
Slice across the grain only when ready to serve, spoon the melted butter over the slices, and add a final pinch of salt if needed.
tips: A dry surface develops better browning.
Thermometer readings are more reliable than timing alone.
Resting is essential for a juicy steak.
commonMistakes: Very cold steaks cook unevenly.
Overcrowding reduces browning.
Cutting immediately releases juices onto the plate.
substitutions: Use strip steaks of similar thickness.
Use olive oil instead of avocado oil.
Replace thyme with rosemary.
storage: Refrigerate cooked steak for up to 4 days.
Reheat briefly at low temperature to limit overcooking.
Freeze wrapped portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Air Fryer Mozzarella Sticks
description: Crunchy homemade air fryer mozzarella sticks with stretchy cheese centers and warm marinara for dipping.
instructions: Cut each cheese stick in half crosswise, arrange the pieces on a tray, and freeze for 30 minutes before beginning the breading process.
Place flour in one shallow dish, whisk eggs with water in a second, and combine both breadcrumbs, Parmesan, and garlic powder in a third.
Coat each frozen cheese piece in flour, dip it completely in egg, and press it firmly into the breadcrumb mixture on every side.
Repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating to create a sealed double crust, paying special attention to covering both cut ends without gaps.
Return all breaded sticks to the freezer for at least 30 minutes, because a firm frozen center gives the crust time to set before cheese melts.
Preheat the air fryer to 390°F, spray the basket and sticks lightly with oil, and arrange one uncrowded layer with room between pieces.
Air-fry for 5 to 7 minutes without turning, removing each stick as soon as the crust is golden and the first tiny spot of cheese appears.
Rest for 2 minutes so the molten centers settle slightly, then serve hot with warmed marinara while the coating remains crisp.
tips: Low-moisture string cheese leaks less.
Double breading seals the cut ends.
Keep breaded sticks fully frozen until cooking.
commonMistakes: Skipping the second freeze causes blowouts.
Thin bare patches allow cheese to escape.
Cooking too long empties the crust.
substitutions: Use gluten-free flour and breadcrumbs.
Replace Parmesan with extra seasoned crumbs.
Serve with pizza sauce instead of marinara.
storage: Freeze uncooked breaded sticks for up to 2 months.
Refrigerate cooked leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat in the air fryer at 350°F until crisp.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: One-Pot Chicken Pasta
description: Creamy tomato one-pot chicken penne with spinach, Parmesan, and a savory weeknight sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Pat the chicken pieces dry and season with half the salt and pepper, keeping the raw chicken and its utensils away from ready-to-eat foods.
Heat oil in a large deep pot over medium-high heat, brown the chicken in one layer, and transfer it to a clean plate before it fully cooks.
Lower the heat to medium, cook the onion until softened, then add garlic and tomato paste and stir until the paste darkens slightly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and broth, scrape every browned bit from the bottom, then stir in dry penne, Italian seasoning, and remaining salt.
Bring to a steady simmer, cover loosely, and cook for about 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes so pasta does not stick to the base.
Return the chicken and collected juices, then simmer until the pasta is tender and the chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 165°F.
Reduce the heat to low, stir in cream, spinach, and Parmesan, and cook only until the spinach wilts and the sauce coats the pasta.
Rest uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken, loosen with a splash of broth if needed, and serve with extra Parmesan and black pepper.
tips: Use a wide heavy pot for even simmering.
Stir regularly because starch settles on the bottom.
Let the finished pasta rest before judging consistency.
commonMistakes: Crowding chicken prevents browning.
Boiling aggressively breaks the sauce.
Adding cream too early can make it separate.
substitutions: Use chicken thighs instead of breast.
Use half-and-half for a lighter sauce.
Replace spinach with chopped kale and cook longer.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Reheat with a splash of broth until 165°F.
Freeze for up to 2 months, although pasta softens.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: One-Pot Taco Pasta
description: Cheesy one-pot taco pasta loaded with seasoned beef, black beans, corn, tomatoes, and tender shells.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat a wide deep skillet over medium-high heat, add the beef and onion, and break the meat into small pieces as it begins to brown.
Cook until no pink remains, carefully spoon off excess grease, then stir in garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, and salt for 30 seconds.
Add diced tomatoes with their juices and the beef broth, scraping the bottom thoroughly to release flavorful browned bits into the liquid.
Stir in the dry pasta shells, bring the mixture to a controlled boil, then reduce to a lively simmer and cover the skillet loosely.
Cook for 10 to 13 minutes, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes so the pasta cooks evenly and cannot weld itself to the bottom.
Fold in the drained black beans and corn, then simmer uncovered until the pasta is tender and the sauce looks slightly looser than desired.
Remove from the heat, stir in one cup cheddar until smooth, and scatter the remaining cheese over the top so it melts without becoming oily.
Rest for 5 minutes as the sauce thickens, then garnish with cilantro and jalapeño and serve while the cheese remains creamy.
tips: Drain excess beef fat before adding liquid.
Stir often once pasta enters the skillet.
The sauce thickens significantly as it rests.
commonMistakes: Using a narrow pan cooks pasta unevenly.
Letting the bottom sit unstirred causes sticking.
Boiling cheese makes the sauce greasy.
substitutions: Use ground turkey instead of beef.
Use kidney beans instead of black beans.
Replace cheddar with Monterey Jack.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Reheat with a splash of broth until steaming hot.
Freeze for up to 2 months with some texture loss.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Slow Cooker Chicken
description: Tender slow cooker chicken thighs with potatoes, carrots, onions, herbs, and a rich savory gravy.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed
instructions: Place the halved potatoes, carrots, and onion in the slow cooker, keeping the pieces thick enough to withstand several hours of cooking.
Pat fully thawed chicken thighs dry, season with salt and pepper, and arrange them over the vegetables without packing them into a solid mass.
Whisk broth, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, thyme, and rosemary until smooth, then pour the mixture around the chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours, avoiding repeated lid lifting because every opening releases heat and extends the cooking time.
Check the thickest chicken pieces with a clean thermometer and continue cooking until they reach at least 165°F and the vegetables are tender.
Transfer chicken and vegetables to a warm platter, then pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan if the slow cooker lacks a high simmer setting.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water, stir the slurry into simmering liquid, and cook for 2 minutes until it becomes a glossy spoon-coating gravy.
Return the gravy to the chicken and vegetables, sprinkle with parsley, and serve hot after checking the final seasoning for salt and pepper.
tips: Use fully thawed chicken for predictable safe cooking.
Cut vegetables into large even pieces.
Keep the lid closed during the slow cook.
commonMistakes: Frozen chicken can remain unsafe too long.
Tiny vegetable pieces turn mushy.
Adding dry cornstarch directly creates lumps.
substitutions: Use bone-in thighs and verify doneness carefully.
Replace potatoes with sweet potatoes.
Use oregano instead of rosemary.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days.
Reheat until chicken reaches 165°F.
Freeze chicken and gravy for up to 3 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Slow Cooker Chili
description: Thick slow cooker beef chili with two kinds of beans, tomatoes, peppers, and deeply layered spices.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, rinsed and drained
Cheddar, sour cream, and scallions, optional
instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces and cooking until no pink remains.
Add onion and bell pepper to the skillet, cook until beginning to soften, then add garlic and stir for another 30 seconds.
Drain excess grease carefully, stir chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, and salt into the beef, and cook until fragrant for one minute.
Transfer the seasoned beef mixture to the slow cooker, then add crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, broth, kidney beans, and pinto beans.
Stir thoroughly, cover, and cook on LOW for 6 to 8 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours without repeatedly lifting the lid.
During the final 30 minutes, uncover only if the chili needs thickening, then cook on HIGH and stir once or twice as moisture evaporates.
Taste carefully and adjust salt or chili powder, adding a small splash of broth only when the chili is thicker than a spoonable consistency.
Ladle into warm bowls and offer cheddar, sour cream, and scallions separately so each serving can be finished just before eating.
tips: Browning beef builds deeper savory flavor.
Rinse canned beans to reduce excess sodium.
Chili tastes even better after an overnight rest.
commonMistakes: Skipping grease draining makes oily chili.
Opening the lid often slows cooking.
Adding too much broth produces soup rather than chili.
substitutions: Use ground turkey instead of beef.
Use black beans for either bean variety.
Add minced jalapeño for extra heat.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Freeze portions for up to 3 months.
Reheat to a rolling simmer or 165°F before serving.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
description: Fall-apart slow cooker pulled pork coated in smoky barbecue sauce and ready for sandwiches or plates.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, excess surface fat trimmed
instructions: Pat the pork shoulder dry and cut it into three or four large chunks so the seasoning covers more surface and the meat cooks evenly.
Combine brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper, then rub the mixture firmly over every side of the pork.
Spread sliced onion across the slow-cooker base, set the seasoned pork on top, and pour vinegar, broth, and Worcestershire around the meat.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 to 10 hours, keeping the lid closed until the pork is very tender and can be separated easily with a fork.
Verify the pork is pull-tender around 195–205°F, then transfer it to a rimmed tray and rest for 10 minutes while skimming fat from the liquid.
Shred the meat with two forks, discard large pockets of fat and connective tissue, and moisten the pork with measured spoonfuls of cooking liquid.
Return the pork to the slow cooker, fold in one cup barbecue sauce, and warm on HIGH for 15 minutes without drowning the meat in sauce.
Taste, add more barbecue sauce as desired, and serve on warm buns with coleslaw or as a plated main while the pork remains juicy.
tips: Pork shoulder has enough fat for tender shredding.
Cook on LOW for the most even texture.
Add cooking liquid gradually after shredding.
commonMistakes: Using pork loin produces drier meat.
Removing the pork before fork-tender leaves tough strands.
Adding all liquid back makes soggy sandwiches.
substitutions: Use bone-in shoulder and allow extra time.
Replace chicken broth with apple juice.
Use your preferred smoky or sweet barbecue sauce.
storage: Refrigerate with some juices for up to 4 days.
Freeze airtight portions for up to 3 months.
Reheat until 165°F, adding sauce if needed.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
